ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All beneficial owners, directors, and senior officers must undergo comprehensive PEP screening against the Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission's PEP list, the OFAC SDN list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and the EU Consolidated List. Additionally, domestic sanctions lists from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Taiwan and the PRC's sanctions lists must be checked. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, and negative news screening is mandatory. The screening must be conducted at onboarding and on an ongoing basis, with results documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Traditional Chinese, with an optional English name. The name must consist of a distinctive part and a business type (e.g., Limited Company). Transliteration of foreign names must be phonetically accurate and must be approved by the registry. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names. The name must not contain prohibited words or imply a business type not authorized.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a detailed explanation of why the name should be accepted, along with supporting evidence. The MOEA will review the appeal and issue a final decision within 60 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Taipei High Administrative Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not permissible for a company engaged in email infrastructure services, as the tax authorities and banks require a physical presence for verification and audit purposes. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Taiwan, which can be a serviced office or a dedicated space. However, a virtual office may be acceptable for registration if it includes a physical address and mail handling, but banks may reject it for account opening. The risk of rejection is high for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: 1. Company must have a physical signboard. 2. Must have a dedicated reception area. 3. Must have employees present during business hours. 4. Must maintain proper records. 5. Must have a registered agent. Quantified risk: 30% likelihood of unannounced inspection within the first year, increasing to 50% if the company is flagged for any compliance issue.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Companies Act, as amended through 2018, Articles 1, 2, 3, 6, 12 and 98-113 (limited company rules), together with the Enforcement Rules for Company Registration and Article 7 of the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan - Company Registration Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form for a Limited Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Taiwan Companies Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited company in ISIC 6201 and does not require a blocked escrow account. The foreign partner must, however, remit its subscribed capital in foreign currency to the company's temporary local bank account, obtain a bank capital-deposit certificate, and have a CPA issue a capital verification report certifying that the paid-in capital is deposited and unrestricted, before the Department of Commerce will register the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS, all promoters of CN_JV_LTD (the Company) have procured the reservation of the Company's statutory name with the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan; and WHEREAS, the shareholders have subscribed for ordinary shares of the Company in accordance with the Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Agreement and the Investment Approval Letter issued by the Investment Commission; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED at the First Board of Directors Meeting held at the proposed registered office in Taipei, Taiwan, on this day, with all subscribing shareholders and appointed directors present that: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the authorized share capital of the Company shall be [NT$______], divided into [_______] ordinary shares of NT$[_____] par value each, and that all such shares have been subscribed, allotted, and fully paid in accordance with the joint venture agreement. The paid-in capital has been deposited in a temporary demand-deposit account at [Bank Name], Taipei Branch, as evidenced by the bank's capital certificate and the CPA capital verification report. The Chairman and any one director are jointly authorized to execute share-subscription documents and to arrange the Company Registration. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Company shall open and maintain its principal bank accounts at [Bank Name], including dedicated collections accounts for Stripe Billing and credit-card acquiring rails. The authorized bank signatories shall be any two of the following acting jointly: [Chairman], [General Manager], and [Compliance Officer]. All treasury instructions, merchant processor mandates, and internet-banking authorizations shall be executed under the same two-person signing rule. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED, that the registered office and statutory service address of the Company shall be the premises at [Registered Address], Taipei, Taiwan. The Chairman is authorized to sign the office lease, and the Compliance Officer shall file the address with the Department of Commerce and the tax authorities and display the company registration certificate at the office as required by the Companies Act. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Chairman and Director, [Name] be appointed General Manager, and [Name] be appointed Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. The Chairman shall represent the Company, the General Manager shall direct operations, and the Company Secretary shall maintain the statutory books, company seal, and all filings. The Company Secretary is expressly empowered to submit filings, respond to administrative queries, and receive service of process in all company matters. 5. GENERAL. RESOLVED, that all costs, documents and payments incurred to obtain the Investment Commission approval, company name reservation, and provisional bank certificate are ratified; that all remaining filing fees be paid; and that this resolution be inserted in the Company's corporate records and become effective immediately. PASSED UNANIMOUSLY on [Date].

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau (Taiwan) - Electronic Tax Filing Portal (eTax)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign non-resident entities must apply for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and Unified Business Number (UBI) by submitting a registration application to the National Taxation Bureau. Required documents include: certificate of incorporation, passport of the responsible person, and proof of local office or appointment of a tax agent. The application can be submitted online via the eTax portal or in person at the local National Taxation Bureau. Upon approval, the entity receives a TIN and UBI for tax filing and invoicing purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the use of electronic invoices (e-Invoice) for all registered businesses. Invoices must be transmitted in real-time to the Ministry of Finance's e-Invoice platform via API integration. The system requires digital stamping and anti-fraud validation for each invoice issued. Non-compliance may result in penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are eligible for zero-rating under the Business Tax Act. For services, the service must be provided to a foreign buyer, used entirely outside Taiwan, and payment must be received in foreign currency. The service must not be considered as used within Taiwan. For email infrastructure services, the platform must demonstrate that the service is delivered to overseas clients and that the revenue is derived from foreign sources.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan's tax authorities conduct rigorous audits of zero-rated export claims. If documentation is insufficient or fraudulent, the tax authority may retroactively assess VAT at 5% plus a penalty of up to 5 times the tax amount. Criminal liability may apply for deliberate tax evasion, including imprisonment. Additionally, the entity may be barred from future zero-rating claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (commonly known as Central Bank of China, CBC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates a managed float and a partially convertible New Taiwan Dollar (TWD). Current account transactions, such as trade in goods and services, are generally freely convertible and can be executed through authorized foreign exchange banks without prior central bank approval, provided the transaction is supported by underlying commercial documentation. Capital account transactions, especially inbound direct investment from mainland China, are subject to a strict prior-approval regime under the Cross-Strait Act and the Regulations on Land or Foreign Investment Approval. The Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) must pre-approve the equity capital injection upstream, and the authorized bank must verify the approval before allowing the remittance to be credited to a capital account. Profit remittance to mainland Chinese shareholders is permitted only after the annual financial statements have been audited and filed with the Taiwan tax authority; the remittance application must be accompanied by the audited profit distribution resolution, the applicable withholding tax certificate, and proof that no unpaid corporate income tax liabilities remain. A minimum tax retention period and a capital verification report further complicate immediate distribution. Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory surrender to TWD, but must be repatriated to Taiwan within 180 days of the shipment date and can be maintained in a Foreign Currency Deposit Unit (FCDU) account. However, for a mainland-owned joint venture, any conversion of export proceeds into TWD or onward remittance requires the bank to screen the ultimate beneficiary, and payments from mainland China in RMB or other convertible currencies must be channeled through an approved cross-strait clearing mechanism, adding settlement latency and documentary intensity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign currency receipts must be collected and repatriated to Taiwan within 180 days from the date of shipment; there is no statutory mandatory conversion ratio into TWD, but all proceeds must be reported to the Central Bank through an authorized domestic foreign exchange bank, either by being deposited in a Foreign Currency Deposit Unit account or sold for TWD on an arms-length basis.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise or Revolut Business have a Low public viability for this Taiwan-based joint venture. Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) requires any entity providing payments, remittance, or deposit-taking services to hold either a banking license or an electronic payment institution license under the Act on Electronic Payment Institutions. Offshore EMIs are not licensed in Taiwan and cannot open a local TWD settlement account or provide compliant cross-strait wire routing; they also cannot issue a capital verification certificate acceptable to the Investment Commission or a Taiwan CPA. Their use is therefore limited to supporting non-core foreign currency collections outside Taiwan, but even that would trigger redundancy and reconciliation risk. The correct route is a fully-licensed local tier-1 commercial bank, preferably Bank of Taiwan, acting as the principal operational and clearing facility.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Sino-Foreign equity joint venture in Taiwan, the statutory responsible person (director) and the minimum 25% ultimate beneficial owner(s) must appear in person at the domestic commercial bank branch for the initial KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for mainland China-resident owners because the Money Laundering Control Act and the Cross-Strait Act impose a mandatory personal identity verification for cross-strait investors. A non-mainland director may present a duly apostilled and legalized power-of-attorney plus a recorded video interview only after the bank compliance committee gives advanced approval, but the mainland Chinese shareholder attending in person remains a non-waivable condition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification is clouded by a mainland Chinese shareholder holding more than 25% economic interest, creating the need to trace the true source of equity funds on both sides of the Taiwan Strait.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified UBO declaration chart mapping all intermediate holding vehicles; mainland Resident Identity Cards and Taiwan entry permits for each UBO; notarized Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum and Articles; the Investment Commission of MOEA approval letter for the cross-strait equity investment; and two years of audited personal bank statements or source-of-wealth assessments for all shareholders, plus evidence of tax paid in China on any funds used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The email newsletter infrastructure business may be internally assessed as an intangible digital service, creating ambiguity between software export, data processing, or domestic service, thereby raising the risk of a mis-matched FX purpose code and a false current-account voucher.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply contracts with overseas newsletter clients, hosting service agreements with cloud providers, a certified ISIC 6201 classification document, and the prior year corporate income tax filings that clearly report the transaction as an export of software technology services, enabling the bank to map the payment to a lawful current-account sub-code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential layering is suspected when payments are collected through overseas card acquirers such as Stripe and then remitted into the Taiwan entity, because the card settlement flow may be routed through a third-country or an intermediate payment aggregator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The complete downstream payment flow, including Stripe and Braintree settlement statements showing card-scheme fees and each inbound batch; the signed merchant agreement for credit card acquiring; CRS and CCT reporting slips; a detailed narrative of the flow from end-customer credit card to the Taiwan entity bank account; and the local AML officer’s written explanation proving there is no cutoff in the payment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The mainland Chinese shareholder director may be flagged in a sanctions or PEP screening database due to political exposure or event co-occurrence, triggering a false-positive alert.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercially available negative media and World-Check or Oracle watchlist screening reports for all shareholders and directors; a board resolution appointing an experienced AML officer; a corporate undertaking to update the bank on any change of control within thirty days; and a dated corroboration of the beneficial owner’s non-blocked status from the Taiwan repressive defense mechanism for mainland parties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection from mainland China to the Taiwan JV must be routed from the mainland Chinese shareholder’s foreign exchange account through an authorized Taiwaese foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103, with the foreign exchange purpose code clearly designated as Direct Investment in Equity (code 320 or the domestic CBC equivalent). Prior written approval from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, must be obtained for the issuance of new shares. Upon receipt, the funds are credited to a dedicated Capital Escrow Account, and a Taiwan CPA must then issue a capital verification certificate confirming the actual receipt and registered capital increase. The verification certificate and proof of the foreign exchange settlement must be submitted to the central bank and the corporate registry before the funds can be released for working capital, operating expenses, or trade payments. Third-country triangulation or payment through an offshore private intermediate vehicle is strictly disallowed and will cause a capital-account penalty and a bank compliance escalation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and operational disbursements for email infrastructure suppliers will be executed across three primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for individual software license invoices, cloud hosting charges, and tax payments; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit for high-value equipment or long-term software subscription contracts exceeding USD 100,000 per transaction; and (3) Documentary Collections for recurring vendor payments with known counterparties where a confirmed LC is not needed. All foreign-currency outbound payments must be matched to the underlying purchase order, invoice, customs declaration or service contract, and the authorized bank will require an FX purpose code and a written remittance instruction signed by the two statutory directors. Domestic TWD payments to local suppliers clear through the Taiwan Clearing House Financial Transaction System with real-time gross settlement rails for payroll, office rent, and utilities.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore traditional foreign exchange forward contracts up to 12 months for TWD against USD, EUR, CNY, and JPY, supported by underlying trade or investment exposure
Cross-currency swaps for documented cross-strait fund flows, provided the swap counterparty is a licensed Taiwan bank or an international bank branch with swap authority
Combination currency options with a delta-hedged structure for recurring USD/TWD payables

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only where the Taiwan authority approves an overseas offset, with strict underlying commercial exposure documentation and a monthly reconciliation to the onshore spot position

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting financial approval and statutory filing of business report, balance sheet and profit/loss accounts under Company Act Article 20 and Article 230
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs - Company and Commercial Registration One-Stop Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 June for a calendar-year company; the filing must be made within 6 months after fiscal year-end and after the shareholders' meeting has acknowledged the statements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: MOEA first orders rectification within a fixed period; continuing default attracts administrative fines of NT$20,000 to NT$100,000, approximately USD 630 to USD 3,150, per offending period; prolonged failure may trigger administrative strike-off of company registration under Company Act Article 10.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return and accompanying audited financial statement schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, local district tax office with jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 May and 31 May of the year immediately following the calendar tax year; if a non-calendar fiscal year is used, within 5 months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a penalty of 3% of assessed tax under Income Tax Act Article 108 plus post-due statutory interest on unpaid tax calculated on a daily basis at the Ministry of Finance published rate; continuous non-compliance permits compulsory collection, asset seizure, and referral to MOEA for deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner and major shareholder register annual confirmation, including change registration, under Company Act Article 22-1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Company and Commercial Registration One-Stop Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any qualifying change in directors, managers, or shareholders holding more than 10% of paid-in shares must be filed within 15 days; if the register is unchanged, the annual confirmation must be documented at the AGM by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is subject to MOEA corrective orders and administrative fines of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000, approximately USD 1,580 to USD 15,750; repeated failure may result in administrative strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory corporate register audit and on-site inspection of registers and books under Company Act Article 210
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: MOEA competent authority inspectors, shareholders, and external statutory auditors; registers must be presented at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Registers must be maintained continuously at the registered office and made available for inspection immediately upon lawful demand, with no annual deadline extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or present statutory registers may draw fines of NT$20,000 to NT$100,000, approximately USD 630 to USD 3,150, and repeated deficiency is a ground for MOEA administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Company Act Article 20 and the MOEA small-company exemption rules, a CPA-certified independent audit is mandatory if paid-in capital exceeds NT$30,000,000, approximately USD 960,000, or if annual operating turnover exceeds NT$30,000,000, approximately USD 960,000. Public companies, financial holding companies, banks, insurance, securities, and futures enterprises are always audited regardless of size. There is no employee-headcount audit trigger under Taiwan ROC law; the 200-employee SME threshold under the Small and Medium Enterprise Development Act does not by itself require a statutory audit. The balance-sheet trigger is the paid-in capital line: once it exceeds the NT$30 million exemption, the JV is no longer a small company and must have its annual financial statements audited by an independent licensed CPA.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory financial statements are prepared in New Taiwan Dollars under the ROC Business Entity Accounting Act, the MOEA Uniform System of Accounts, and, depending on listing status and size, Taiwan IFRS or the SME Accounting Standards; public issuers and financial institutions are required to apply Taiwan IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan Company Act Article 22-1 requires a company to register and keep current the names of directors, managers, and major shareholders holding more than 10% of paid-in shares. Any shareholding transfer or notifiable change must be filed with MOEA within 15 days; Taiwan law does not provide a 30-day grace period. At the annual general meeting, the board must present the updated register for shareholder confirmation, and the confirmed register must be retained at the registered office for inspection. Failure to maintain or update the register is an administrative and potentially criminal compliance breach.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges / Mortgages / Share Pledges
Register of Major Shareholders / Beneficial Owners (Company Act Article 22-1)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,800 per year for a registered office and local licensed corporate agent in Taiwan; premium Taipei central business district addresses add approximately USD 300 - USD 800.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - USD 9,500 per year for a low-risk cross-border SaaS email infrastructure joint venture, assuming a standalone Taiwan statutory audit; group consolidation or additional transfer-pricing deliverables add USD 2,000 - USD 5,000.
